cards.name: Color
cards.summary: Non-separable mode: keeps the luminosity of the artwork underneath and takes hue and saturation from the object, so it tints whatever is below without changing its light and shade. On the plate the gradient recolours the orange box, blue star and gradient circle magenta-to-cyan at their own brightness; the near-black type and strokes stay very dark but pick up a tint (dark purple under magenta, navy mid-way, almost black under cyan), since only pure black cannot be tinted.
use_for: tint a placed greyscale photo or texture with a brand colour
colour-wash mixed artwork to one hue family for a poster background
quick colourway previews without editing the fills
avoid: Black and white below cannot be tinted (their luminosity stays 0 or 100%); for permanent, editable colour changes use Edit > Edit Colors > Recolor Artwork.

Adobe documents that Difference, Exclusion, Hue, Saturation, Color and Luminosity do not blend spot colours; convert spots to process or use another mode. Adobe also advises a rich CMYK black instead of 100% K black, which knocks out the colour beneath with most modes.

Where the object sits over empty artboard there is nothing to blend with and it shows its own colours (the artboard is not a white object); put a white or coloured shape behind it if it must react to the 'paper'.
cards.equivalents_note: CorelDRAW: Transparency tool > Uniform Transparency, Merge mode Color (cdrMergeColor, 14) (script: shape.Transparency.MergeMode).

cards.name: Color Burn
cards.summary: Darkens the artwork underneath to reflect the object's colour by increasing the contrast between them: white in the object changes nothing, saturated colours drive the backdrop to deep, saturated darks. On the plate (the box sits under the magenta-to-violet third of the rectangle, the star under the middle, the circle under the blue-to-cyan third) the box burns to pure red (255,0,0) and the blue star to pure blue (0,0,255); the gradient circle keeps orange-red on its left and burns to near-black navy (0,22,81) under the cyan end; the black type and strokes stay black.
use_for: deepen and saturate the shadows of artwork or a placed photo with a colour shape
moody colour grading of poster backgrounds
burnt-edge vignette shapes over textures
avoid: Harsh: clips darks to black and over-saturates quickly; for a gentler darken use Multiply at lower opacity.
Light, pale objects do almost nothing (white is neutral).

Where the object sits over empty artboard there is nothing to blend with and it shows its own colours (the artboard is not a white object); put a white or coloured shape behind it if it must react to the 'paper'.

cards.name: Color Dodge
cards.summary: Brightens the artwork underneath to reflect the object's colour by decreasing the contrast between them: black in the object changes nothing, bright colours blow the backdrop out toward highlights. On the plate (the box sits under the magenta-to-violet third of the rectangle, the star under the middle, the circle under the blue-to-cyan third) the box dodges to salmon and pale pink (255,127,127 to 255,169,174) and the star to a lighter sky blue, and the white blow-out is on the gradient circle under the blue-to-cyan end; the near-black type and strokes light up (type to a strong blue, the zigzag magenta to blue to cyan) because the gradient's blue channel is 80-99 % and dodge divides the backdrop by 1 minus the object.
use_for: glow and light-leak shapes over darker artwork
punchy highlight accents on illustrations and type
neon-style colour pops on mid-tone backgrounds
avoid: Clips to white fast; for soft lightening use Screen at lower opacity.
Only pure black below stays put; near-black reacts wherever the object has a channel near 100%.

Where the object sits over empty artboard there is nothing to blend with and it shows its own colours (the artboard is not a white object); put a white or coloured shape behind it if it must react to the 'paper'.

cards.name: Darken
cards.summary: Per colour channel keeps whichever is darker, the object or the artwork beneath: lighter parts of the object vanish where the backdrop is darker, darker parts replace it. Because it works per channel, mixes can give a third colour: on the plate (the box sits under the magenta-to-violet third of the rectangle, the star under the middle, the circle under the blue-to-cyan third) the box turns red to brown (243,11,26 to 176,71,26) under the magenta-to-violet part, the star stays blue, and the gradient circle mixes to green on its left and dark navy (9,53,82) under the cyan end; black type and strokes stay black.
use_for: drop a light-background scan or texture over artwork so only its darker marks show
screen-print / riso style overlapping colour layers
combine line-art layers keeping the darkest strokes
avoid: Illustrator has no whole-colour Darker Color mode (Photoshop does); Darken compares R, G and B separately, so expect new colours where hues differ.
Over white the object just shows; it only differs from Normal where the backdrop has darker channels.

Where the object sits over empty artboard there is nothing to blend with and it shows its own colours (the artboard is not a white object); put a white or coloured shape behind it if it must react to the 'paper'.

cards.name: Difference
cards.summary: Per channel subtracts the darker of object and backdrop from the lighter: white in the object inverts what is below, black changes nothing, giving negative, high-contrast, acid colours. On the plate (the box sits under the magenta-to-violet third of the rectangle, the star under the middle, the circle under the blue-to-cyan third) the box turns teal-blue to indigo (12,111,177 to 79,51,191), the star maroon to olive-brown (122,1,33 to 67,51,21), the gradient circle magenta-violet to pale pink-beige, and the near-black type takes the gradient's own colours.
use_for: white shapes or type that invert the artwork underneath
psychedelic / acid poster colour clashes
checking registration of two copies of the same art (matching areas go black)
avoid: Adobe documents that Difference, Exclusion, Hue, Saturation, Color and Luminosity do not blend spot colours; convert spots to process or use another mode. Adobe also advises a rich CMYK black instead of 100% K black, which knocks out the colour beneath with most modes.
Blending runs in the document colour mode (File > Document Color Mode), so RGB and CMYK documents give different results; proof in the output mode.

Where the object sits over empty artboard there is nothing to blend with and it shows its own colours (the artboard is not a white object); put a white or coloured shape behind it if it must react to the 'paper'. A white object over empty artboard therefore does not invert the paper.

cards.name: Exclusion
cards.summary: Like Difference but lower in contrast: white in the object inverts the backdrop, black leaves it unchanged, and mid-tones of the object pull the result toward grey. On the plate (the box sits under the magenta-to-violet third of the rectangle, the star under the middle, the circle under the blue-to-cyan third) the box turns blue to periwinkle (12,123,188 to 79,126,199), never pink since it does not reach the cyan end; the star turns olive (147,118,33 to 105,132,21), the gradient circle lavender to pale pink-beige, and the near-black type lavender to periwinkle, close to the gradient itself.
use_for: subtler inverted-colour effects than Difference
retro / risograph style colour-clash backgrounds
invert-on-overlap type treatments with softer mid-tones
avoid: With pure primary / secondary colours in the object it looks identical to Difference; it only reads differently in in-between colours.

cards.name: Hard Light
cards.summary: Multiplies or screens depending on the object: channels lighter than 50% grey lighten (screen) the backdrop, darker ones darken (multiply), 50% grey is neutral, so the object's colour dominates like a harsh spotlight (Overlay with the roles swapped). On the plate the pure magenta and cyan ends look almost like Normal, since 0% and 100% channels override the backdrop, while the middle of the gradient lets the artwork through with its blue channel pushed to full (orange box goes pink, black type goes blue).
use_for: apply a texture or pattern with strong contrast over artwork
spotlight / lighting shapes on illustrations
contrasty colour overlays where the object's colour should dominate
avoid: Saturated, near-black or near-white objects mostly hide what is below; to keep the artwork's detail use Overlay or Soft Light.

Where the object sits over empty artboard there is nothing to blend with and it shows its own colours (the artboard is not a white object); put a white or coloured shape behind it if it must react to the 'paper'.

use_for: shift the hue of colourful artwork or placed photos without touching lightness or saturation
quick colourway variations for patterns and packaging
unify differently coloured elements to one hue
avoid: No effect on neutral artwork; to tint greys use Color.
